- The only CausalSmith imports you may add or retain are same-run modules under `CausalSmith.Substrate.MeasurableCompactArgminSelection.*`. ## Instructions
Prove the sole `sorry` in `CausalSmith/Substrate/MeasurableCompactArgminSelection/Main.lean` without changing or weakening either public theorem. You may add private helper declarations and targeted Mathlib imports in this substrate tree; split a genuinely independent helper chain if the file approaches 900 lines. Do not import research/paper modules or introduce axioms, admits, hidden assumptions, uniqueness, or convexity.

Search Mathlib locally before coding. Useful existing ingredients include `TopologicalSpace.denseSeq`/`exists_dense_seq`, `Dense.ciInf'`, `Measurable.iInf` or `Measurable.isGLB`, `IsCompact.exists_isMinOn`, `IsCompact.finite_cover_balls`, `Measurable.find`, `cauchySeq_of_le_geometric_two`, and `measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable`.

A concrete route is:
1. Prove a private measurable-value lemma for any jointly measurable objective with continuous action sections over a fixed nonempty compact set. Represent the minimum through a countable dense sequence in the compact subtype; use density plus continuity (`Dense.ciInf'` may avoid manual approximation) and compact attainment.
2. Let the argmin fiber be `{y ∈ K | f (x,y) = value x}`. Prove measurable hit predicates for this fiber with finitely many closed-ball constraints. Encode the constraints by a nonnegative jointly measurable penalty such as `|f-value|` plus positive parts of distance excesses. Its compact minimum is measurable and equals zero iff the constrained fiber is nonempty; compactness supplies attainment.
3. Choose finite geometric-radius nets of `K`. Recursively select the least net point whose ball meets the argmin fiber and, after the base step, whose witnessing minimizer is also within the previous approximation radius. Use the hit lemma and `Measurable.find` (or a finite measurable fold) to prove every approximation measurable. Maintain a minimizer within radius `2⁻ⁿ`; consecutive approximations are then bounded by the sum of adjacent radii.
4. Obtain a pointwise Cauchy limit in Euclidean space, prove it belongs to the closed argmin fiber using the nearby exact minimizers and radii tending to zero, and use `measurable_of_tendsto_metrizable` for measurability.

Equivalent faithful Brown--Purves/Arsenin--Kunugui specializations are welcome if Lean is cleaner. Preserve the existing nearest-point proof. Exit only after `lake env lean CausalSmith/Substrate/MeasurableCompactArgminSelection/Main.lean` has no errors, source grep finds no `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom`, and `#print axioms` for both public theorems reports only standard Lean axioms.

Use the lean-lsp MCP tools to develop/check your proof (diagnostics/goal). When done, output a
